title: Psychology: Professional Foundations
description: Twenty-four-unit professional-style psychology curriculum covering research methods, neuroscience, cognition, learning, development, social and clinical psychology, ethics, and Catholic human-formation integration.
creditNote: 48 internal Save One Soul formation credits (24 units × 2). Professional-style in breadth and study method; non-accredited and not a psychology degree, licence or clinical qualification.

units.title: Foundations of psychological science
units.label: Professional-style psychology formation
objectives: Explain the major concepts and evidence in scientific method, operational definitions, replication and limits.
Distinguish established findings, plausible interpretations and unsupported claims.
Apply the material to a fictional case while respecting clinical and ethical limits.
paragraphs: This unit studies scientific method, operational definitions, replication and limits. Professional psychological reasoning begins by defining constructs carefully, examining evidence and specifying the population and context to which a conclusion applies. It avoids turning one experiment, brain image, personal story or theoretical school into a total explanation of a person.

The central disciplinary lens is research methods. Students should compare competing explanations, identify measurement limits and ask what evidence would change the conclusion. Biological, cognitive, behavioural, developmental, social and cultural accounts can be complementary rather than mutually exclusive.

Application requires role clarity. Educational study can improve observation, communication and help-seeking, but it does not confer authority to diagnose, prescribe, conduct psychotherapy or replace qualified assessment. Where distress, impairment, safeguarding concerns or medical questions arise, professional referral takes priority.

lectureSections.title: Professional study method
paragraphs: For each topic, move from definition to evidence, from evidence to interpretation, and from interpretation to bounded application. Record limitations and alternative explanations explicitly.

lectureSections.title: Integration with human formation
paragraphs: When psychology intersects with moral or spiritual language, distinguish spontaneous emotion and automatic processing from deliberate judgment and choice. Avoid using neuroscience to assign guilt, sanctity, vice or virtue.

methodNotes: Use peer-reviewed or authoritative educational sources where possible.
Do not infer diagnosis from a vignette, symptom list or brain region.
Separate description of mechanisms from moral or spiritual evaluation.
units.researchTask: Prepare a 1,000-word literature-style note on foundations of psychological science, summarizing evidence, limitations, one controversy and one practical implication.
units.assignment: Write a 700–1,000 word professional-style response to a fictional case involving foundations of psychological science. Include observations, hypotheses, evidence needed, ethical limits and an appropriate next step.

quiz.question: Which approach best fits professional psychological study?
options: Define constructs, evaluate evidence and state limits
Assign a diagnosis from one clue
Treat one theory as explaining every person
quiz.explanation: Professional reasoning requires operational clarity, evidence and explicit limits.

quiz.question: What does completion of this self-study course authorize?
options: Independent clinical practice
No clinical licence; it supports education and appropriate referral
Prescription of treatment
quiz.explanation: This is non-accredited education and does not confer clinical competence.

objectives: Explain the major concepts and evidence in attachment, cognition, language, temperament and contextual development.
Distinguish established findings, plausible interpretations and unsupported claims.
Apply the material to a fictional case while respecting clinical and ethical limits.
paragraphs: This unit studies attachment, cognition, language, temperament and contextual development. Professional psychological reasoning begins by defining constructs carefully, examining evidence and specifying the population and context to which a conclusion applies. It avoids turning one experiment, brain image, personal story or theoretical school into a total explanation of a person.

The central disciplinary lens is development. Students should compare competing explanations, identify measurement limits and ask what evidence would change the conclusion. Biological, cognitive, behavioural, developmental, social and cultural accounts can be complementary rather than mutually exclusive.

Application requires role clarity. Educational study can improve observation, communication and help-seeking, but it does not confer authority to diagnose, prescribe, conduct psychotherapy or replace qualified assessment. Where distress, impairment, safeguarding concerns or medical questions arise, professional referral takes priority.

lectureSections.title: Professional study method
paragraphs: For each topic, move from definition to evidence, from evidence to interpretation, and from interpretation to bounded application. Record limitations and alternative explanations explicitly.

lectureSections.title: Integration with human formation
paragraphs: When psychology intersects with moral or spiritual language, distinguish spontaneous emotion and automatic processing from deliberate judgment and choice. Avoid using neuroscience to assign guilt, sanctity, vice or virtue.

methodNotes: Use peer-reviewed or authoritative educational sources where possible.
Do not infer diagnosis from a vignette, symptom list or brain region.
Separate description of mechanisms from moral or spiritual evaluation.
units.researchTask: Prepare a 1,000-word literature-style note on development: infancy and childhood, summarizing evidence, limitations, one controversy and one practical implication.
units.assignment: Write a 700–1,000 word professional-style response to a fictional case involving development: infancy and childhood. Include observations, hypotheses, evidence needed, ethical limits and an appropriate next step.

quiz.question: Which approach best fits professional psychological study?
options: Define constructs, evaluate evidence and state limits
Assign a diagnosis from one clue
Treat one theory as explaining every person
quiz.explanation: Professional reasoning requires operational clarity, evidence and explicit limits.

quiz.question: What does completion of this self-study course authorize?
options: Independent clinical practice

mid.question: Correlation by itself establishes causation.
options: True
False
mid.explanation: Causal inference requires design and alternative explanations.

mid.question: A brain region can directly reveal moral guilt.
options: True
False
mid.explanation: Neuroscience does not measure moral culpability.

mid.question: A valid assessment requires attention to reliability and validity.
options: True
False

mid.question: Automatic processing means all later behaviour is uncontrollable.
options: True
False
mid.explanation: Automaticity and absence of agency are not identical.

mid.question: Culture and context can alter how behaviour is interpreted.
options: True
False
mid.explanation: Context is essential to responsible interpretation.

final.question: Professional role boundaries require referral when needs exceed competence.
options: True
False
final.explanation: Referral protects the person and the helper.

final.question: A symptom list alone is enough for diagnosis.
options: True
False

final.question: Evidence-based care means one method works equally for everyone.
options: True
False
final.explanation: Evidence, clinical expertise and individual context all matter.

final.question: Psychological mechanisms and moral evaluation are related but not interchangeable.
options: True
False
final.explanation: They address different levels of explanation.

options: True
